check_download_milestone.description: Check whether a package's downloads in a day, any 7 days or any 30 days have reached a number, such as a million a month, and on which day they got there. 'newly_reached' is true only on the first day the total reaches it in the days PyPI Stats keeps, so a workflow that runs daily celebrates once, not again each time a quiet weekend takes the total back under and the next day lifts it over. Also says how far there is to go and the best total in the days PyPI Stats keeps. Counted from the daily figures without mirror traffic. PyPI Stats keeps about six months, so all-time totals are out of reach. No API key required.

check_download_milestone.name: check_download_milestone

check_unusual_downloads.description: Check whether a package's latest downloads are out of the ordinary, for an alert: a sudden spike when a big project starts depending on it, or a drop when an install breaks. The latest day is compared with the same weekday in earlier weeks, because downloads always fall at the weekend, or the latest 7 days with the weeks before. Comes back with the change in percent and a status of spike, drop or normal, so a condition only has to check 'unusual'. Mirror traffic is left out. No API key required.

Answers 'are we still ahead of them?' in one step rather than several. Between two and ten packages; a package PyPI Stats has no figures for is listed as missing rather than failing the step. get_download_history.description: Get a package's daily download series, up to the 180 days PyPI Stats keeps. Comes back with the total, the average per day, the busiest day, and the same figure for the equal window immediately before, so a step can say 'up 12% on the month before' rather than only quoting a number. Roll the rows up by week or month for a chart, or ask for no series at all when only the totals matter. Mirror traffic is left out by default. No API key required.
get_download_history.name: get_download_history

get_download_summary.description: Get everything a maintainer's weekly or monthly report needs about a package in one step: downloads in the last day, week and month; the total and daily average over the days you choose, and how that compares with the same number of days before; the share coming from Python 3 and from Python 2, every Python version's share; and every operating system's share. Two requests, made one after another. Every number, the last day, 7 days and 30 days included, is added up from PyPI Stats' daily figures and ends on the latest day it has counted, because its own figures for the last week and month can lag weeks behind. Mirror traffic is left out. No API key required.
get_download_summary.name: get_download_summary

get_recent_downloads.description: Get how many times a package was downloaded from PyPI in the last day, the last week and the last month. All three numbers come back every time; the period you choose picks which one lands in the single 'downloads' field, so a threshold or an alert has one number to read. Mirror traffic is already excluded, so these are real installs. The starting point for 'how is my package doing?'. No API key required.

description: Read PyPI download statistics from a workflow. Get a package's downloads over the last day, week and month, or its full daily series over the 180 days PyPI Stats keeps, with the total, the average per day, the busiest day and how the window compares with the one before it. Split those downloads by Python major version, by minor version to see whether 3.9 can be dropped, or by operating system to see which wheels are worth building. Compare several packages side by side, ranked with each one's share. Get a maintainer's summary in one step, check whether the latest downloads are a spike or a drop for an alert, and check when a package reaches a download milestone. Mirror traffic is excluded by default, so the figures are real installs. Every action reads: nothing here changes anything. No account or API key required.
